title: Hof backup manifest
description: Written into the staging tree (ADR 0006's own Backup Flow step 8) and so into every destination's own snapshot alongside it - the one document restore reads BEFORE trusting anything else in the snapshot. Carries the same digest quartet state-v1.schema.json already uses so restore can verify this snapshot's own generated config against a real, independently-verifiable signed historical release lock, without ever having to trust the snapshot's own unsigned content alone.

backupId.description: This plan's own backupId (backup-plan-v1) - a domain-separated digest of installationId+generation+backupPolicyId+backupSequence, never a content-id of this manifest itself (scripts/backup-ids.mjs's computeBackupId).

consistencySet.description: Same shape as backup-plan-v1's own consistencySet (copied, not $ref'd) - exactly what this snapshot actually contains, so restore can confirm the volume set it's about to recreate matches what this manifest claims before restoring a single byte.

sanitizedManifestDigest.description: sha256 of the sanitized copy of services.yml actually written into this snapshot's own staging tree (secretRef names only, never a resolved secret value) - a digest, not a boolean, so its presence is itself the proof of inclusion; there is no legitimate real backup where this artifact is absent.

recoveryKitDigest.description: sha256 of the recovery-kit-v1 document actually written into this snapshot's own staging tree - the same digest restore-plan-v1's own recoveryKitDigest must match before restore ever trusts the kit it obtained separately. A digest, not a boolean: its presence is the proof of inclusion, and restore can confirm the two match rather than merely trusting an unverifiable claim that some kit was included.
